FRNSC 100: This course is designed for students to step into the role of a criminalist ¿ one who performs the scientific examination of evidence - as they process a case from start to finish over the semester.
FRNSC 200: This course offers an exploration of the science, management, and investigative techniques for the field of crime scene investigation.
FRNSC 210: Practices of forensic science including documentation, microscopy, communication of results, and integration of concepts from other sciences, mathematics, and statistics.
FRNSC 294: Supervised student activities on research projects identified on an individual or small-group basis.
FRNSC 295: Supervised off-campus, nongroup instruction including field experiences, practica, or internships.
FRNSC 296: Creative projects, including research and design, that are supervised on an individual basis and that fall outside the scope of formal courses.
FRNSC 297: Formal courses given infrequently to explore, in depth, a comparatively narrow subject which may be topical or of special interest.
FRNSC 400: Introduction to courtroom proceedings and testimony as they related to forensic science.
FRNSC 410: Principles of crime scene investigation with emphasis on scientific philosophy, concepts, and procedures.
FRNSC 411: Laboratory-based examination of forensic evidence; microscopy, classification and identification.
FRNSC 412: Laboratory-based examination of forensic evidence; microscopy, classification and identification.
FRNSC 413: Laboratory-based examination of forensic evidence; biological fluid identification, hair microscopy.
FRNSC 415W: Laboratory course covering crime scene investigation with emphasis on scientific philosophy, concepts, procedures, problem solving, and hands-on activities.
FRNSC 419: Laboratory-based examination of forensic evidence; firearms, tool marks, shooting reconstruction and related evidence.
FRNSC 420: Classroom discussions will focus on advanced aspects of molecular biology, including as they relate to forensic DNA analysis.
FRNSC 421W: Classroom discussions will focus on the application of molecular biology techniques to forensic DNA analysis.
FRNSC 425: FRNSC 425 will provide the student with understanding in essential instrumentation for chemical analysis.
FRNSC 427W: Analytical and instrumental methods used in the forensic sciences with special emphasis on the analysis and characterization of trace evidence.
FRNSC 460: This course will introduce students to the concepts of medicolegal death investigation and the operations of a medical examiner or coroner's office.
FRNSC 475: Presentation and discussion of special issues in forensic science; extension and application of background knowledge to unusual topics and cases.
FRNSC 485: This course will prepare students to make the transition to professional careers in forensic science and allied fields.
FRNSC 485W: Advanced concepts in criminalistics as they apply to criminal and civil investigations.
FRNSC 490: This course will explore the knowledge and methods relevant to traceology and the scientific reconstruction of events.
FRNSC 494: Supervised student activities on research projects identified on an individual or small-group basis.
FRNSC 496: Creative projects, including research and design, that are supervised on an individual basis and that fall outside the scope of formal courses.
FRNSC 497: Formal courses given infrequently to explore, in depth, a comparatively narrow subject which may be topical or of special interest.
